reading:g114p2.title: The Pros and Cons of Horror Movies
reading:g114p2.text:
第 1 段Typically featuring zombies and serial killers, horror movies are too frightening to be fun for some people. But many others enjoy a good fear spectacle, and line up to see the latest scary movie. Given the variations in preferences, new studies have started to untangle the benefits and risks of horror movies.

第 2 段One benefit of horror movies revolves around the concept of so-called “safe fear.” When watching a frightening film, people are in the comfort of their own home or theater seats rather than under the threat of any real danger. In a controlled environment, these films may actually reduce the negative impact on viewers and help them become tougher. Secondly, as people are drawn into the story, they tend to take the perspective of the characters and rehearse the plot unconsciously. Researchers believe that viewers are learning vicariously this way, picking up tips on how to handle threats in the real world. In addition, studies show that the thrill and excitement linked with scary films can be therapeutic: It allows viewers to release bottled-up emotions and experience a sense of relief after the movie is over. This probably explains why during the COVID-19 pandemic, horror and pandemic thrillers were the most-watched movies on digital movie apps.

第 3 段However, researchers also find that horror movies can have negative effects on some people. People who are more sensitive to anxiety can panic after viewing a thriller. For those with unpleasant experiences, trauma may be triggered by the themes and images in the movies, which could make their symptoms worse. Furthermore, watching horror movies can disturb sleep patterns, as the residual fear and anxiety they evoke may keep people awake all night, thus leading to fatigue and irritability the following day. Finally, specialists warn that frightening films can have a negative impact on children. Children under 14 who watch horror movies have a greater chance of developing anxiety later in adulthood. Worse yet, exposure to graphic violence and bloodshed can make them less sensitive to real-life violence and more accepting of aggression.

reading:g113p2.title: Painter Thomas Moran and Yellowstone
reading:g113p2.text:
第 1 段Thomas Moran, a famous painter in the 19th century, played an important role in the establishment of American national parks. His vivid paintings brought the splendor of the extraordinary landscapes before the eyes of American people, thus setting the stage for the regions to be widely recognized and officially established as national parks.

第 2 段Moran came to the United States at age 7 with his family and settled in Philadelphia. They came from northwest England, the blackened heart of the Industrial Revolution: Its main street was “a dark, unattractive hole” and the river running through it was a string of dirty water. That was all the nature that Moran knew. Moran began painting by age 15, inspired by the landscape paintings of the British master J.M.W. Turner. There was plenty of landscape for him to paint in America, much different from his hometown. Showing great talent in painting, Moran was soon hired as an illustrator at Scribner’s Monthly, and later appointed chief illustrator by age 34. In 1871, he was appointed to illustrate The Wonders of Yellowstone, a story by Nathaniel P. Langford, who had participated in an expedition to Yellowstone. Captivated by the utterly fantastic sights Langford described, Moran became eager to see this odd territory for himself.

第 3 段In 1871 Moran joined the first US government survey of the Yellowstone region with photographer William Henry Jackson. For two weeks he filled his sketchbook with the landscape’s most stunning sights. Moran’s watercolors—the first color renderings of the area—as well as Jackson’s photos and the survey results were presented to the Congress. His powerful images of Yellowstone fired the imagination of Congress members. In March 1872, lawmakers officially made Yellowstone a national park, the world’s first.

第 4 段Before Moran arrived, Yellowstone in the popular imagination was a harsh, wild place with hot water and steam coming out of hellish holes in the ground. Since the painter’s work appeared, Yellowstone National Park has come to be known as a picturesque wonderland. By the time Moran died, he had painted a dozen other areas that would become national parks or monuments.

reading:g112p2.title: Elephants and Tea Gardens
reading:g112p2.text:
第 1 段When you enjoy your morning cup of tea, you are probably not aware that those tea leaves can mean injury, or even death, for Asian elephants roaming Indian tea gardens.

第 2 段In the Indian state of Assam, growing numbers of tea farms are destroying the Asian elephant’s habitats and endangering their population. Much of the forest land where tea is grown in Assam is flat and thus farmers must dig drainage trenches to prevent water from accumulating and hurting the shrubs. The trenches, however, can be death traps for the elephants. Since the elephants need to use tea plantations as landmarks when navigating forests, they almost inevitably have to move through the farms. Moreover, because there are fewer humans around, pregnant females often use tea-growing areas as safe shelters to give birth. But baby elephants, not used to negotiating rough ground, may easily fall into the trenches and get hurt; and once injured, they might not be able to climb out. When mothers try to dig their babies out, both may be trapped and smothered by thick mud. Furthermore, elephants are known to resist leaving their sick or dying behind, and a herd may linger at a trench with a trapped baby for hours, reluctant to move on until all hope is lost.

第 3 段Is it possible for elephants to coexist with the prosperous tea business? Elephant Friendly Tea is an organization that takes the initiative to make it possible. The organization encourages consumers to choose brands that take precautions to protect elephants and has set up a certification program to reward tea growers who are doing it right. Until now, only smaller tea brands have been certified, but awareness is growing. The organization believes that people may be motivated to buy elephant-friendly brands when they know more about the risk tea can pose to these endangered animals.

reading:g111p2.title: The Evolution of the Hard Hat
reading:g111p2.text:
第 1 段A hard hat is a helmet used mostly at worksites to protect the head from injuries due to falling objects. Since its introduction in the early 20th century, the headgear has saved countless lives and is considered the number one safety tool for construction workers.

第 2 段The hard hat was invented in 1919 by Edward W. Bullard, who had just returned from World War I. Before the war, workers used to smear their hats with coal tar for protection of their head. Bullard, having witnessed the life-saving power of the metal helmet in the War, decided to produce a head protection device that was affordable for every worker and lightweight enough to be worn all day long. The Hard Boiled Hat was thus born, using steamed canvas and leather, covered with black paint, and featuring a suspension system to reduce impact. Soon, hard hats became widely used. The headgear was later made mandatory at construction sites in major construction projects, such as the Hoover Dam in 1931 and the Golden Gate Bridge in 1933.

第 3 段Over the past century, hard hats have advanced considerably, evolving from canvas and leather to aluminum, fiberglass, and, eventually, to thermoplastic. Recently, new models have been introduced and accessories added to meet the needs of laborers working on various job sites. For instance, a ventilated hard hat was developed to keep wearers cooler, and see-through face shields were attached to better see the hazards lurking above. Today, attachments include radios, sensors, cameras, and a lot more. A common color code has also been developed for recognizing people and their roles on site. Yellow is used for general laborers and contractors, white (or sometimes black) for supervisors and managers, and green for inspectors and new workers.

第 4 段New products continue to expand the market. Global sales of hard hats totaled USD 2.1 billion in 2016, and are expected to reach USD 3.19 billion in 2025.

reading:g110p2.title: The History of Passports
reading:g110p2.text:
第 1 段The concept of a travel document, which shows a person is under a ruler’s protection while in a foreign land, has probably existed since rulers and states were first invented. But the earliest mention of an object which we might recognize as a passport appeared in about 450 B.C. The Hebrew Bible states that Nehemiah, an official serving King Artaxerxes of ancient Persia, asked permission to travel to Judah. The King agreed and gave Nehemiah a letter “to the governors of the province beyond the river,” requesting safe passage for him as he travelled through their lands.

第 2 段Later, in the medieval Islamic Caliphate, a form of passport was the bara’a, a receipt for taxes paid. Only people who paid their taxes were permitted to travel to different regions of the Caliphate. In medieval Europe, on the other hand, travel documents were issued by local authorities, and generally contained a list of towns and cities which the document holder was permitted to enter or pass through. On the whole, documents were not required for travel to seaports, which were considered open trading points, but documents were required to travel inland from seaports.

第 3 段King Henry V of England is credited with having invented the first true passport, as a way of helping his subjects prove who they were in foreign lands. The earliest reference to these documents is found in a 15th-century Act of Parliament, while the term “passport” came into use about a century later. Nevertheless, passports were not generally required for international travel until the First World War. It was at this time that passports as we would recognize them today began to be used.

reading:g109p2.title: The Profession of Marine Pilot
reading:g109p2.text:
第 1 段Ships are the lifeline of trade among countries. Almost everything, from food to machinery, comes by way of the sea in huge ships piloted by captains. But the captain of a ship is responsible for guiding the vessel until they hit a port, waiting to enter the harbor. The task of bringing the ship into the harbor and anchoring it is taken up by a different captain. This captain is called a marine pilot.

第 2 段A marine pilot is a boat pilot with specialized knowledge of a particular port or harbor. The pilot is needed to direct large ships into a port, where there are often deep water channels surrounded by shallower seabeds. Without the services of a marine pilot, docking ships would be hazardous. There would be a real chance of running aground and damaging the ship and the cargo, some of which might be dangerous if released into a water-based ecosystem.

第 3 段In addition to the shallower seabeds, tide and wind pose further challenges for bringing ships into a port. During different tides, currents may change from one direction to the other. The same strategy for docking a vessel during an incoming tide may not work during an outgoing tide. Also, the wind can significantly alter the direction of the ship and how it reacts, adding to the difficulty of anchoring the ship.

第 4 段Marine pilotage is a job that requires a high degree of proficiency as well as quick and independent thinking. Above all, it is about risk management. A marine pilot goes on board at a crucial time and controls the vessel based on his or her knowledge of the port and the situation at hand. The pilot is responsible for not only the safety of the ship but also the protection of the port and the marine environment.

reading:g108p2.title: Totem Poles in North America
reading:g108p2.text:
第 1 段Totem poles in North America are poles or posts carved with symbols or figures by Aboriginal peoples of the Northwest Coast. Carved from large, straight trees and painted vibrant colors, the totem poles are not just unique works of art. The coastal peoples have long passed on knowledge from generation to generation through oral traditions, and totem poles were the traditional way of telling the story of an individual family or clan.

第 2 段The totem pole can be grouped into specific categories, depending on its location and the occasion for which it was carved. Welcome poles were traditionally placed on village beachfronts to greet visitors arriving by canoe. Inside the homes of high-ranking chiefs is where house poles were found. The family’s history was carefully carved into each pole. Placed along the rear or front walls of a house, house poles also helped to support the main beam of the roof.

第 3 段Memorial poles stood in front of a house. They were erected in memory of a deceased chief or a high-ranking clan member. The poles depicted the person’s accomplishments or family history. Mortuary poles were also raised to honor the dead, but they differed from memorial poles, having a burial box placed at the top of the pole. Inside the burial box were the remains of the deceased.

第 4 段While many of these poles can still be found in various locations on the west coast of North America, there is one pole that can now only be found in a museum—the shame pole. Traditionally, shame poles were carved for a chief to embarrass and ridicule another who had done something wrong. Once the wrong was made right, the pole was taken down.

第 5 段Totem poles are important expressions of specific Aboriginal cultures. Despite the threats posed by cultural and political encroachment of colonial forces, the art of totem pole carving has survived. Aboriginal carvers continue to carve totems as symbols of their cultural pride and clan kinship.

reading:g107p2.title: West Nile Virus
reading:g107p2.text:
第 1 段West Nile is a tropical disease that begins in birds, which pass it on to mosquitoes that then go on to infect human beings with a bite. Most people who contract West Nile do not experience any symptoms at all, but, if they do, symptoms typically develop between 3 to 14 days after a mosquito bite. About 1 in 5 persons suffers fever, headaches, and body aches, usually lasting a week or so. A far less lucky 1 in 150 experiences high fever, tremors, paralysis, and coma. Some—especially the elderly and those with weak immune systems—die.

第 2 段That is what made the major outbreaks of West Nile in the U.S. in the summer of 2012 so scary. The situation was particularly bad in Dallas, Texas, where the West Nile virus killed 10 people and sickened more than 200. The city declared a state of emergency and began aerial spraying of a pesticide to kill the mosquitoes, even though residents argued that the pesticide could be more dangerous than the disease.

第 3 段Why was the summer of 2012 so hospitable to the West Nile virus and the mosquitoes that carry it? Blame the weather. An extremely mild winter allowed more mosquitoes than usual to survive, while the unusually high temperatures in that scorching summer further increased their number by speeding up their life cycle. The economic crisis may have also played a role: Homeowners who were not able to pay their bank loans were forced to abandon their properties, sometimes leaving behind swimming pools that made excellent mosquito breeding grounds.

第 4 段The severity of tropical diseases is also a matter of whether governments are capable—and willing—to defend their populations against infections. Dallas County was not doing some of the key things to slow the spread of West Nile, such as testing dead birds and setting mosquito traps to test for the presence of the disease. Tropical infections are thus as much related to government inaction as they are to climate.

reading:g106p2.title: Capoeira
reading:g106p2.text:
第 1 段Capoeira is a martial art that combines elements of fight, acrobatics, drumming, singing, dance, and rituals. It involves a variety of techniques that make use of the hands, feet, legs, arms, and head. Although Capoeira appears dancelike, many of its basic techniques are similar to those in other martial arts.

第 2 段Capoeira was created nearly 500 years ago in Brazil by African slaves. It is believed that the martial art was connected with tribal fighting in Africa, in which people fought body to body, without weapons, in order to acquire a bride or desired woman. In the sixteenth century, when the Africans were taken from their homes to Brazil against their will and kept in slavery, Capoeira began to take form among the community of slaves for self-defense. But it soon became a strong weapon in the life-or-death struggle against their oppressors. When the slave owners realized the power of Capoeira, they began to punish those who practiced it. Capoeiristas learned to camouflage the forbidden fights with singing, clapping, and dancing as though it were simply entertainment.

第 3 段At first, Capoeira was considered illegal in Brazil. However, a man known as Mestre Bimba devoted a great deal of time and effort to convincing the Brazilian authorities that Capoeira has great cultural value and should become an official fighting style. He succeeded in his endeavor and transformed the martial art into Brazil’s national sport. He and Mestre Pastinha were the first to open schools, and the Capoeira tree grew, spreading its branches across the world. Nowadays, it is performed in movies and music clips. Capoeira is also believed to have influenced several dancing styles like breaking and hip-hop.

reading:g105p2.title: The Story of a Young Inventor
reading:g105p2.text:
第 1 段Like many other five-year-olds, Jeanie Low of Houston, Texas, would use a stool to help her reach the bathroom sink. However, the plastic step-stool she had at home was unstable and cluttered up the small bathroom shared by her whole family. After learning of an invention contest held by her school that year, Jeanie resolved to enter the contest by creating a stool that would be a permanent fixture in the bathroom, and yet could be kept out of the way when not in use.

第 2 段Jeanie decided to make a stool attached to the bathroom cabinet door under the sink. She cut a plank of wood into two pieces, each about two feet wide and one foot long. Using metal hinges, Jeanie attached one piece of the wood to the front of the cabinet door, and the second piece to the first. The first piece was set just high enough so that when it swung out horizontally from the cabinet door, the second piece would swing down from the first, just touching the ground, and so serving as a support for the first piece of the wood. This created a convenient, sturdy platform for any person too short to reach the sink. When not in use, the hinges allowed the two pieces of wood to fold back up tightly against the cabinet, where they were held in place by magnets. Jeanie called her invention the “Kiddie Stool.”

第 3 段Jeanie’s Kiddie Stool won first place in her school’s contest. Two years later, it was awarded first prize again at Houston’s first annual Invention Fair. As a result, Jeanie was invited to make a number of public appearances with her Kiddie Stool, and was featured on local TV as well as in newspapers. Many people found the story of the Kiddie Stool inspiring because it showed that with imagination, anyone can be an inventor.

reading:g104p2.title: The Problem of Overtreatment
reading:g104p2.text:
第 1 段When it comes to medical care, many patients and doctors believe “more is better.” But what they do not realize is that overtreatment—too many scans, too many blood tests, too many procedures—may pose harm. Sometimes a test leads you down a path to more and more testing, some of which may be invasive, or to treatment for things that should be left alone.

第 2 段Terrence Power, for example, complained that after his wife learned she had Wegener’s disease, an uncommon disorder of the immune system, they found it difficult to refuse testing recommended by her physician. The doctor insisted on office visits every three weeks, even when she was feeling well. He frequently ordered blood tests and X-rays, and repeatedly referred her to specialists for even minor complaints. Even when tests came back negative, more were ordered, and she was hospitalized as a precaution when she developed a cold. She had as many as 25 doctor visits during one six-month period. The couple was spending about $30,000 a year for her care.

第 3 段After several years of physical suffering and near financial ruin from the medical costs, the couple began questioning the treatment after consulting with other patients in online support groups. “It’s a really hard thing to determine when they’ve crossed the line,” Mr. Power said. “You think she’s getting the best care in the world, but after a while you start to wonder: What is the objective?” Mr. Power then spoke with his own primary care doctor, who advised him to find a new specialist to oversee Mrs. Power’s care. Under the new doctor’s care, the regular testing stopped and Mrs. Power’s condition stabilized. Now she sees the doctor only four or five times a year.

reading:g103p2.title: The Success of the Emanuel Brothers
reading:g103p2.text:
第 1 段Below is an excerpt from an interview with Zeke Emanuel, a health-policy expert, on his famous brothers.

第 2 段Interviewer: You’re the older brother of Rahm, the mayor of Chicago, and Ari, an extremely successful talent agent. And you’re a bioethicist and one of the architects of Obamacare. Isn’t writing a book about how great your family is a bit odd?

第 3 段Zeke: I don’t write a book about how great my family is. There are lots of idiocies and foolishness—a lot to make fun of in the book. I wrote Brothers Emanuel because I had begun jotting stories for my kids. And then we began getting a lot of questions: What did Mom put in the cereal? Three successful brothers, all different areas.

第 4 段I: To what do you attribute the Emanuel brothers’ success?

第 5 段Z: I would put success in quotes. We strive. First, I think we got this striving from our mother to make the world a better place. A second important thing is you never rest on the last victory. There’s always more to do. And maybe the third important thing is my father’s admonition that offense is the best defense. We don’t give up.

第 6 段I: Do you still not have a TV?

第 7 段Z: I don’t own a TV. I don’t own a car. I don’t Facebook. I don’t tweet.

第 8 段I: But you have four cell phones.

第 9 段Z: I’m down to two, thankfully.

第 10 段I: Your brothers are a national source of fascination. Where do you think they’ll be in five years?

第 11 段Z: Ari will be a superagent running the same company. Rahm would still be mayor of Chicago. I will probably continue to be my academic self. The one thing I can guarantee is none of us will have taken a cruise, none of us will be sitting on a beach with a pina colada.

reading:g102p2.title: The Problem of Space Junk
reading:g102p2.text:
第 1 段Space is where our future is—trips to the Moon, Mars and beyond. Most people would think that aside from comets and stars there is little else out there. But, since our space journey started we have left so much trash there that scientists are now concerned that if we don’t clean it up, we may all be in mortal danger.

第 2 段The first piece of space junk was created in 1964, when the American satellite Vanguard I stopped operating and lost its connection with the ground center. However, since it kept orbiting around the Earth without any consequences, scientists became increasingly comfortable abandoning things that no longer served any useful purpose in space.

第 3 段It is estimated that there are currently over 500,000 pieces of man-made trash orbiting the Earth at speeds of up to 17,500 miles per hour. The junk varies from tiny pieces of paint chipped off rockets to cameras, huge fuel tanks, and even odd items like the million-dollar tool kit that astronaut Heidemarie Stefanyshyn-Piper lost during a spacewalk.

第 4 段The major problem with the space trash is that it may hit working satellites and damage traveling spacecraft. Moreover, pieces of junk may collide with each other and break into fragments which fall back to the Earth. To avoid this, scientists have devised several ways for clearing the sky. Ground stations have been built to monitor larger pieces of space trash to prevent them from crashing into working satellites or space shuttles. Future plans include a cooperative effort among many nations to stop littering in space and to clean up the trash already there.

reading:g114p1.title: The Invention History of Traffic Lights
reading:g114p1.text:
第 1 段While waiting to cross the street at busy intersections, have you ever wondered who invented the traffic light? Most people credit the first traffic light to Nottingham engineer John Peake Knight. A railway manager, Knight specialized in designing the signaling system for Britain’s growing railway network in the 1860s. He saw no reason why this could not be adapted for use on the busy London intersections. Thus, he proposed a signaling system based on the railway movable-arm signal: Arms extending horizontally commanded drivers to stop, whereas arms lowered to a 45-degree angle told drivers to move on, resembling a traffic director’s gestures. Red and green gas lamps were added to the signal for use at night. A police officer was stationed by the side to operate the system.

第 2 段Knight’s traffic signal was installed near London’s Westminster Bridge in December 1868, but the system was short-lived. A gas leak one month later caused an explosion in the lights, injuring the policeman operating it. Deemed a public hazard, the project was immediately dropped, and traffic lights were banned until their return in 1929 back to the British streets.

第 3 段In the early 1900s, versions of the British traffic lights appeared in big cities in America, where traffic was on a sharp rise. Systems using movable arms were popular in Chicago, while those using the red and green lights were adopted in San Francisco. Patents with innovations on Knight’s ideas were filed nationwide. A major breakthrough was the yellow light invented by a Detroit police officer William Potts. Installed in Detroit in 1920, Potts’ three-color system allowed for the added signal “proceed with caution” to be displayed.

第 4 段Now, with the emergence of self-driving cars, researchers have begun to suggest that traffic signals are no longer necessary. Intersections will operate in a way that cars automatically adjust their speed to cross through, while maintaining safe distances from other vehicles. In the near future, we may experience a brand new form of traffic management!

reading:g112p1.title: The History of the Hula Hoop
reading:g112p1.text:
第 1 段When did people first experience the joy of the hula hoop? Although the term did not emerge until the 18th century, toy hoops twirled around the waist, limbs, or neck can be traced back to ancient times. As early as 1000 BC, Egyptian children played with hoop toys of dried grapevine. They threw, jumped, and slung them around their bodies as we do today. They also struck them with sticks to roll them down the road. Hoop rolling was also popular in ancient Greece. Their hoops, often made of metal, were not merely toys for Greek children but served as exercise devices as well.

第 2 段In the 14th century, hoops were popular as a form of recreation in Great Britain. The craze for hoops even resulted in dislocated backs and heart attacks, according to medical records. The term “hula,” however, did not enter the English language until the 1700s, when British sailors first witnessed hula dancing in the Hawaiian Islands. Though no hoops were used, the movements of the ritual dances looked very similar to those in hooping. Thus “hula” and “hoop” came together, resulting in the term “hula hooping.”

第 3 段Hoops spun their way through the cultures of pre-colonial America as well. Often considered as representing the circle of life, hoops featured prominently in the ritual dances of Native Americans. Dancers used small reed hoops as symbolic representations of animals such as eagles or snakes. With very rapid movements, they used the hoops to construct the symbolic forms around their bodies.

第 4 段The hula hoop gained international popularity in the late 1950s, when a plastic version was successfully marketed by California’s Wham-O toy company. Twenty-five million plastic hoops were sold in less than four months. The hula hoop “fad” is still going strong today.

reading:g110p1.title: Prickly Pear Cactus as Renewable Energy
reading:g110p1.text:
第 1 段The prickly pear cactus is such a powerful symbol in Mexico that it occupies a prime spot on Mexico’s national flag. The plant was considered sacred by the ancient Aztecs, and modern-day Mexicans eat it, drink it, and even use it in medicines and shampoos. Now scientists have come up with a new use for the bright green plant: producing renewable energy.

第 2 段Known locally as nopal, the prickly pear is farmed on a massive scale in Mexico. Over the years, only the edible soft inner flesh has been used. The cactus’s thick outer layer (i.e., husk), with all those spines, had always been viewed as a waste product until researchers developed a biogas generator to turn the husks into electricity.

第 3 段The pilot project dedicated to developing the cactus biogas generator began in the south of Mexico City. The area produces 200,000 tons a year of prickly pear cactus—up to 10 tons of which ends up as waste on the floor of the cactus market each day. Then, a local green energy startup company got the idea to turn that waste into energy. The generator is now in place at the cactus market, where the vendors are enthusiastic about this new way to utilize the tons of cactus husks that once went directly into the trash.

第 4 段The prickly pear has a number of advantages over other biofuel crops, such as wheat, sugarcane, and soybeans. For one thing, only the husk of the cactus is used for generating biofuel, while its inner flesh is still preserved for food. Therefore, using the plant as a fuel source will not put pressure on food prices. Moreover, the cactus requires minimum water, and thus is not grown on traditional agricultural pasture. This means that no increased competition arises for the water or land presently used for food production.

第 5 段The project in Mexico City has brought new hope to reducing the use of fossil fuels. If it can be expanded, the prickly pear could be the key to Mexico’s energy future.

options.C: COVID-19 was an important source of inspiration for horror movies.
options.D: Watching horror movies may have a long-term effect on personality.

questions.explanation: 小時候看恐怖片，成年後比較容易焦慮，對暴力也變得麻木、更能接受攻擊行為，這些都是對性格的長期影響。(A) 原文只說兒童，選項擴大成大多數愛看恐怖片的人；(C) 照抄第 2 段的 COVID-19，但原文說疫情期間大家愛看恐怖片，不是疫情帶給恐怖片靈感；(B) 文章好處、壞處都談，沒說哪一邊比較多。

questions.prompt: How does the author develop the ideas in this passage?

options.A: By defining and illustrating a concept.
options.B: By showing opposing views of an issue.
options.C: By presenting cause and effect of a problem.
options.D: By providing steps for settling a disagreement.

questions.explanation: 第 1 段最後一句預告要談好處和風險，第 2 段講好處，第 3 段用 However 轉到壞處，兩段立場相反。(A) 照抄第 2 段的 concept，但 safe fear 只是第一個好處，不是全文的寫法。(C) 文章確實談看恐怖片的影響，但同時列出好處和壞處，沒有把看恐怖片當成一個問題，去分析它的成因和後果；(D) 第 1 段說每個人喜好不同，但全文沒有化解什麼爭議，也沒有列出任何步驟。

questions.prompt: What can we learn from the passage?

options.A: How national parks around the world were established.
options.B: How Yellowstone’s natural features were formed.
options.C: Why Moran’s family moved to the United States.
options.D: Why Moran started painting Yellowstone.

questions.explanation: 他接下為 Langford 的黃石故事畫插圖的工作，書裡描述的奇景又讓他著迷，他才想親眼去看，這就是他開始畫黃石的原因。(A) 文章只講黃石一座公園的設立經過；(C) 只說他隨家人移民，沒說為什麼搬家；(B) 黃石的地貌怎麼形成，文章沒提。

questions.prompt: Why does the author use “the blackened heart” in paragraph 2 to describe Moran’s hometown?

options.A: The place was severely polluted.
options.B: The town was filled with darkened holes.
options.C: There were many evil-hearted industry owners.
options.D: The laborers mostly wore dark and dirty uniforms.

questions.explanation: 冒號後面就是解釋：街道又暗又難看，河是一條髒水，工業革命把這裡燻黑了，所以 blackened 指的是汙染嚴重。(B) 照抄 hole，但「洞」是形容大街的比喻；(C) 照抄 heart，但這裡的 heart 是「核心地帶」，不是人心。(D) 文章沒有提到工人的制服，blackened 形容的是整個地方，不是工人穿的衣服。

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is true about the Yellowstone National Park?

options.A: Its establishment was proposed by Langford.
options.B: Americans knew little about its beauty before the 1870s.
options.C: The government project was started due to its rich natural resources.
options.D: It was the only national park established because of Moran’s works.

questions.explanation: Moran 1871 年去黃石之前，一般人以為那裡荒涼可怕，可見並不知道黃石的美。(A) 照抄 Langford，他只是寫了探險故事；(C) 照抄 government，原文說政府考察後設立公園，沒說是因為天然資源；(D) 照抄 national park，但第 4 段說 Moran 還畫了另外十二處後來成為國家公園或保護區的地方。

questions.prompt: What can be inferred from the passage?

options.A: Scribner’s Monthly was a magazine promoting national parks.
options.B: Moran had visited Yellowstone before he started painting its landscapes.
options.C: Color photos were not common when Moran started painting Yellowstone.
options.D: Watercolor was the most popular form of landscape painting in the 19th century.

questions.explanation: 同行的 Jackson 拍了照片，最早的彩色圖像卻是 Moran 的水彩畫，可見當時的照片不是彩色的。(B) 方向相反：他在 1871 年親自去黃石之前，已經在為黃石的故事畫插圖；(D) 照抄 watercolors，但文章沒有比較哪一種風景畫最流行；(A) 文章沒說那份雜誌在推廣國家公園。

questions.prompt: Why do farmers in Assam dig trenches in tea gardens?

options.A: To protect tea trees.
options.B: To trap elephants.
options.C: To expand tea farms.
options.D: To mark boundaries of tea gardens.

questions.explanation: 挖排水溝是為了不讓積水傷害茶樹，原文的 shrubs 在選項換成 tea trees。(B) 照抄下一句的 trap，但溝渠變成大象的死亡陷阱是意外，不是挖溝的目的。(C) 第 2 段開頭說茶園愈來愈多，那是茶園擴張破壞大象的棲地，挖溝並不能擴大茶園；(D) 的 mark 呼應同一段的 landmarks，可是拿茶園當地標的是大象，溝渠也不是用來標出茶園的邊界。

questions.prompt: Why are baby elephants easily injured in the Assam tea gardens according to the passage?

options.A: They cannot find a safe shelter when climbing out of the trenches.
options.B: They cannot locate the landmarks while trying to navigate forests.
options.C: They are trapped by the sharp branches of the tea trees.
options.D: They have difficulties moving around the uneven fields.

questions.explanation: negotiate 在這裡是「通過、走過」，不是談判；小象不習慣走崎嶇的地面，在選項換成在不平的田裡行動有困難，rough 換成 uneven。(A) 照抄 safe shelter 和 climb out，但安全的庇護所是母象選來生產的地方；(B) 照抄 landmarks，那是成年大象辨認方向用的。(C) 文章沒有提到茶樹的枝條，小象受傷是因為掉進溝渠。

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements about elephants and the tea gardens is true according to the passage?

options.A: The elephants use the trenches to roam around the tea gardens.
options.B: The fast growth of the tea gardens destroys the elephants’ food source.
options.C: Elephants are unwilling to leave their injured members behind in the tea gardens.
options.D: Pregnant elephants avoid delivering babies in the tea gardens for fear of being disturbed.

questions.explanation: resist leaving 換成 unwilling to leave，sick or dying 換成 injured members。(D) 照抄 Pregnant，但原文正好相反，母象常到茶園生產；(A) 照抄 trenches，溝渠是陷阱，不是大象移動的路線；(B) 文章說茶園破壞的是棲地，沒說食物來源。

questions.prompt: What does “it” in the last paragraph refer to?

options.A: To certify elephant-friendly trenches and organizations.
options.B: To reward tea growers for protecting the environment.
options.C: To encourage consumers to choose high-quality brands.
options.D: To create a win-win situation for elephants and tea farms.

questions.explanation: make it possible 回應前一句的問句 Is it possible …：讓大象和茶葉產業共存，也就是兩全其美。(A) 照抄同一段的 certification，可是第 3 段說認證的對象是做好保護措施的茶農和茶葉品牌，不是溝渠，也不是組織；(B)、(C) 照抄後一句組織的做法，那是達成目標的方法，不是 it 本身；(C) 的 high-quality 原文也沒提。

questions.prompt: Which of the following aspects about hard hats is NOT discussed in the passage?

options.A: Their functions.
options.B: Their appearances.
options.C: Their materials.
options.D: Their limitations.

questions.explanation: 有提到的三個面向：第 1 段保護頭部是 (A) 功能，第 2、3 段的帆布、皮革、鋁、塑膠是 (C) 材質，第 2 段的黑漆和第 3 段的顏色標示是 (B) 外觀。安全帽有什麼缺點或限制，文章沒提。

questions.prompt: In what order did the following protective hats appear? a. fiberglass hats b. hats with see-through shields c. hats with canvas and leather d. hats with tar over them

options.A: d → c → a → b
options.B: c → d → b → a
options.C: c → b → a → d
options.D: d → c → b → a

questions.explanation: 依時間排：一戰前塗煤焦油（d）、1919 年帆布和皮革（c）、之後的玻璃纖維（a）、近年才加上的透明面罩（b）。選項照用原文的材料名稱，難處在第 3 段的 Recently 把面罩排到最後。(B)、(C) 把帆布和皮革排在煤焦油之前，(C) 還把煤焦油放到最後，可是第 2 段說塗煤焦油是一戰前的做法；(B)、(D) 把透明面罩排在玻璃纖維之前，順序也不對。

questions.prompt: According to the passage, which of the following statements is true about the hard hat?

options.A: Global sales have doubled every ten years.
options.B: The inspiration came from the inventor’s wartime experience.
options.C: It was standard equipment for construction workers in the 1920s.
options.D: Different colors are used in different industries to signal the roles of people on site.

questions.explanation: Bullard 在戰場上看到金屬頭盔救人，才決定做安全帽，就是靈感來自他的戰時經歷。(C) 照抄 construction，但工地規定一定要戴是 1931、1933 年的事，不是 1920 年代；(D) 照抄 roles，但顏色區分的是工地上的職務，不是不同的產業；(A) 2016 年到 2025 年預估從 21 億到 31.9 億美元，不是每十年翻倍。

questions.prompt: Which of the following words are used in the passage to refer to the hard hat? a. tool b. code c. device d. helmet e. accessory f. headgear

options.A: a, b, d, e
options.B: a, c, d, f
options.C: c, d, e, f
options.D: a, d, e, f

questions.explanation: 作者換了四個說法來指安全帽，避免一直重複 hard hat：helmet、headgear、tool、device。code 指的是顏色標示，accessory 是加裝在安全帽上的配件，都不是安全帽本身：(A) 混進了 code 和 accessory，(C)、(D) 混進了 accessory。

questions.prompt: How is the information in the passage organized?

options.A: In order of time.
options.B: By cause and effect.
options.C: In order of importance.
options.D: By definition and illustration.

questions.explanation: 全文依時間往下走：西元前 450 年的尼希米、中世紀的伊斯蘭國家和歐洲、15 世紀的亨利五世、一百年後出現 passport 這個詞，到第一次世界大戰，所以是依時間順序排列。交卷後「這一篇的文章結構」也把這篇歸為時序發展。(B) 文章沒有分析護照出現的原因和結果；(C) 各個時期只是依先後排列，沒有比較哪一個比較重要；(D) 第 1 段第一句雖然說明旅行文件是什麼，後面各段卻是依年代往下講，不是舉例說明一個定義。

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is true about the earliest travel document?

options.A: It was issued by the king of Judah.
options.B: It was given to an official of Persia.
options.C: It appeared more than three thousand years ago.
options.D: It served to invite people to travel beyond the river.

questions.explanation: 國王把信交給為古波斯國王效力的官員尼希米。(A) 照抄 Judah，那是尼希米要去的地方，發信的是波斯國王；(D) 照抄 beyond the river，那封信是寫給河那邊的省長，請他們放行，不是邀人去旅行；(C) 西元前 450 年距今大約兩千五百年，不到三千年。

questions.prompt: When did the term “passport” start being used?

options.A: In about 450 B.C.
options.B: During World War I.
options.C: In the 16th century.
options.D: During King Henry V’s reign.

questions.explanation: 15 世紀的法案再過大約一百年，就是 16 世紀，要自己推算。(D) 照抄 King Henry V，那是發明護照的人，不是這個詞出現的時間；(B) 第一次世界大戰是護照普遍使用的時間；(A) 照抄第 1 段的 450 B.C.。

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT mentioned in the passage as a form of passport?

options.A: A letter.
options.B: A receipt.
options.C: A proof of identity.
options.D: A list of seaports.

questions.explanation: 有提到的三種：第 1 段國王的信（(A) letter）、第 2 段的繳稅收據（(B) receipt）、第 3 段亨利五世的護照幫人證明身分（(C) proof of identity）。(D) 把第 2 段的 list 和 seaports 拼在一起：歐洲的文件列的是城鎮，前往海港反而不需要文件。

questions.prompt: What is the passage mainly about?

options.A: A special profession.
options.B: Shipping and trading.
options.C: Guidelines for safe docking.
options.D: Protection of the marine environment.

questions.explanation: 第 1 段引出引水人這個職業，第 2–3 段說這份工作為什麼需要、難在哪裡，第 4 段總結這份工作的要求和責任，所以全文介紹的是一種特殊的職業。(B) 航運與貿易是第 1 段開頭的引子，範圍比引水人大得多，太過廣泛；(C) 船隻靠港的難處只在第 2、3 段，文章也沒有列出什麼準則，(D) 海洋環境的保護只在第 2 段和第 4 段末尾帶到，兩個都過於狹隘。

questions.prompt: Which of the following is part of the knowledge that a marine pilot must have?

options.A: The value of the ships.
options.B: The content of the cargo.
options.C: The weather conditions.
options.D: The diversity of marine life.

questions.explanation: 第 3 段說潮汐和風會改變船的方向，第 4 段說引水人要依當下的狀況操控船隻，所以天氣狀況是必備的知識，原文的 wind 在選項換成概括的 weather conditions。(B) 的 cargo 取自第 2 段，那裡講的是擱淺時貨物會受損，不是引水人要懂貨物內容。(A) 文章沒有提到船的價值；(D) 第 4 段說引水人要保護海洋環境，這是職責，文章沒有說引水人要懂海洋生物的多樣性。

questions.prompt: What does “a crucial time” in the last paragraph refer to?

options.A: When the vessel hits a flat.
options.B: When the channel is not deep enough.
options.C: When there is a collision of two ships.
options.D: When a ship is waiting to enter the port.

questions.explanation: 第 1 段說船長把船開到港口、等候進港時，就換引水人接手，這正是引水人登船的關鍵時刻；harbor 在選項換成 port。(B) 的 channel 取自第 2 段，講的是港口的地形，不是登船的時間點。(A) 的 hit 照抄第 1 段 until they hit a port，flat 是淺灘，船撞上淺灘就是第 2 段說的擱淺，那是引水人要避免的意外，不是引水人登船的時候；(C) 文章沒有提到兩艘船相撞。

questions.prompt: How does the author conclude the passage in the last paragraph?

options.A: By adding new details.
options.B: By predicting future development.
options.C: By summarizing the main points.
options.D: By giving advice to the general public.

questions.explanation: 末段把前面講過的內容再收一次：專業知識對應第 2 段，迅速獨立的判斷對應第 3 段的潮汐和風，船和海洋環境的安全對應第 2 段的擱淺與貨物外洩，所以是總結重點。(A) 末段沒有新的細節；(B) 末段沒有談未來的發展；(D) 末段講的是引水人的職責，沒有給一般大眾任何建議。

questions.prompt: Which of the following is the best title for this passage?

options.A: Totem Poles, the Legends of Aboriginal Peoples
options.B: Totem Poles: Their Functions
options.C: Totem Poles, Symbols of Historical Resistance
options.D: Totem Poles: Their Designs

questions.explanation: 第 1 段說圖騰柱不只是藝術品，也是講述家族故事的方式；第 2–4 段依位置和用途，介紹迎賓柱、屋柱、紀念柱、墓葬柱和羞辱柱各有什麼作用，所以最好的標題是圖騰柱的功能。(D) 柱子的雕刻和色彩只在第 1 段帶到，(C) 抵抗殖民勢力只在第 5 段提到，都過於狹隘；(A) 圖騰柱記錄的是家族和氏族的歷史，文章沒有談原住民的傳說，偏離主題。

questions.prompt: How is the information about totem poles organized in Paragraphs 2 to 4?

options.A: In order of importance.
options.B: In order of time.
options.C: By cause and effect.
options.D: By classification.

questions.explanation: 第 2 段一開頭就說圖騰柱可以依位置和場合分成幾類（can be grouped into specific categories），接著第 2 到 4 段逐一介紹迎賓柱、屋柱、紀念柱、墓葬柱和羞辱柱，所以是分類。交卷後「這一篇的文章結構」也把這篇歸為分類。(A) 文章沒有比較哪一種圖騰柱比較重要；(B) 各種柱子是依類別介紹，不是依出現的先後；(C) 文章說明各種柱子立在哪裡、為什麼而刻，但沒有把一件事當成原因、另一件事當成結果來推論。

questions.prompt: Which of the following is located at the edge of a body of water?

options.A: The house pole.
options.B: The shame pole.
options.C: The memorial pole.
options.D: The welcome pole.

questions.explanation: 題幹的 at the edge of a body of water（水邊），是第 2 段 beachfronts（海灘邊）的換句話說；立在海灘邊、迎接划獨木舟來訪客人的是迎賓柱。(A) 屋柱在酋長家中，(C) 紀念柱立在房屋前面，(B) 羞辱柱現在只在博物館裡，都不在水邊。

questions.prompt: Which is closest in meaning to the word “encroachment” in the last paragraph?

options.A: Invasion.
options.B: Appointment.
options.C: Objection.
options.D: Enrichment.

questions.explanation: Despite 表示讓步：儘管殖民勢力帶來威脅，雕刻藝術仍然流傳下來。會對原住民文化構成威脅的，是殖民勢力在文化和政治上的侵逼，所以 encroachment 最接近 invasion（侵略、侵入）。(D) enrichment 是使豐富，方向正好相反；(B) 任命、(C) 反對都談不上威脅。

questions.prompt: What is this passage mainly about?

options.A: West Nile and methods to fight it.
options.B: West Nile and governmental efficiency.
options.C: West Nile and the conditions its virus thrives in.
options.D: West Nile and its relation to tropical diseases.

questions.explanation: 第 1 段說明西尼羅病毒怎麼傳染、有哪些症狀；第 2 段說 2012 年達拉斯疫情嚴重；第 3 段說天氣和經濟危機讓蚊子大量繁殖；第 4 段說政府不作為也讓疾病擴散。第 3、4 段講的都是病毒在什麼條件下容易蔓延，所以是 (C)。(A) 對抗疾病的方法只在第 2、4 段帶到（空中噴藥、檢驗死鳥），(B) 政府效率只在第 4 段談到，都過於狹隘；(D) 把話題拉大到熱帶疾病整體，太過廣泛。這一題考後有人主張 (B) 也對，大考中心邀集專家討論後維持 (C)，說明試題文章是從原始報導大幅刪節改寫而成，作答要以考卷上這篇文章的脈絡為準。

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is true about West Nile?

options.A: Its symptoms usually appear within two weeks.
options.B: It is spread through air and water in tropical areas.
options.C: Over 20% of people who contract it will suffer severe symptoms.
options.D: It comes from direct human contact with birds infected with the virus.

questions.explanation: 第 1 段說症狀通常在蚊子叮咬後 3 到 14 天出現，也就是兩週以內；選項把 typically develop 換成 usually appear。(B) 照抄 tropical，但原文說病毒由鳥傳給蚊子、蚊子再叮人，不是經由空氣和水傳播；(D) 照抄 birds，人類是讓帶病毒的蚊子叮了才感染，不是直接接觸鳥類；(C) 大約五分之一的人只是發燒、頭痛，出現高燒、癱瘓這類嚴重症狀的是每 150 人中的 1 人，遠低於 20%。

questions.prompt: What did Dallas County do to fight off West Nile?

options.A: They sprayed pesticide from the air.
options.B: They asked citizens to stay away from dead birds.
options.C: They encouraged citizens to get vaccinations.
options.D: They drained the swimming pools in the county.

questions.explanation: 第 2 段說達拉斯市宣布緊急狀態，開始從空中噴灑農藥（aerial spraying of a pesticide），選項換成 sprayed pesticide from the air。(B) 照抄第 4 段的 dead birds，原文說達拉斯郡沒有檢驗死鳥，那是該做卻沒做的事；(D) 照抄第 3 段的 swimming pools，廢棄的游泳池是蚊子的繁殖場所，文章沒說郡政府去處理；(C) 接種疫苗文章沒提。

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a reason why Dallas was hit most seriously in the U.S. in 2012?

options.A: The increasing population in Texas raised the risk of contracting the disease.
options.B: The government did not issue a warning about the disease in time.
options.C: The residents worried about the county’s decision and action.
options.D: The weather of the previous winter was not as cold as usual.

questions.explanation: 第 3 段說極為溫和的冬天讓比平常更多的蚊子活了下來，an extremely mild winter 在選項換成 not as cold as usual。(C) 照抄第 2 段的 residents，居民擔心的是噴藥的危險，這是政府處理疫情時的爭議，不是疫情嚴重的原因；(A) 照抄 Texas，文章沒說德州人口增加；(B) 第 4 段批評的是郡政府沒有檢驗死鳥、設置捕蚊器，不是沒有及時發布警告。

questions.prompt: What is the passage mainly about?

options.A: The history of Capoeira.
options.B: The values of Capoeira.
options.C: The contribution of Capoeira.
options.D: The techniques of Capoeira.

questions.explanation: 第 1 段介紹卡波耶拉是什麼；第 2 段講它將近五百年前由巴西的非洲奴隸創造，從自衛變成反抗的武器；第 3 段講它從違法到成為巴西國技，再傳遍世界。全文依時間講卡波耶拉的發展，所以是 (A)。(D) 技巧只在第 1 段介紹，(B) 文化價值和 (C) 對舞蹈風格的影響只在第 3 段提到，都過於狹隘。

questions.prompt: Which of the following will probably NOT be found in the performance of Capoeira?

options.A: Singing with drums.
options.B: Sweeping with the legs.
options.C: Stabbing with swords.
options.D: Striking with the hands.

questions.explanation: 第 1 段說卡波耶拉結合擊鼓和歌唱（drumming, singing），是 (A)；技巧會用到手、腳、腿（hands, feet, legs），是 (B) 用腿掃和 (D) 用手打。文章沒有提到刀劍，第 2 段反而說它源自赤手空拳、不用武器的部落格鬥，所以 (C) 用劍刺最不可能出現。

questions.prompt: What is the author’s attitude toward Capoeira as a sport?

options.A: Admiring.
options.B: Objective.
options.C: Doubtful.
options.D: Harsh.

questions.explanation: 全文介紹卡波耶拉的起源、演變和現況，只陳述事實，沒有表達作者自己的好惡；說到起源和影響，還用 It is believed、is also believed to 這類保留的說法。作者的態度是客觀的，所以是 (B)。(A) 欣賞容易誤選：第 3 段說卡波耶拉有很高的文化價值，但那是 Mestre Bimba 說服政府的理由，不是作者的評價；(C) 懷疑和 (D) 嚴厲，文章都找不到依據。

questions.prompt: According to the passage, which of the following statements is true about Capoeira?

options.A: It was greatly influenced by modern dancing styles.
options.B: It was initially created as a type of dance and ritual.
options.C: It was mainly performed to protect a bride or desired woman.
options.D: It was officially recognized in Brazil through the effort of Mestre Bimba.

questions.explanation: 第 3 段說 Mestre Bimba 花了大量時間和心力說服巴西政府，最後成功讓卡波耶拉成為巴西國技，選項把 convincing the Brazilian authorities 換成 officially recognized in Brazil。(A) 照抄 dancing styles，原文說的是卡波耶拉影響了霹靂舞、嘻哈舞，選項把影響的方向說反了；(C) 照抄第 2 段的 bride or desired woman，那是非洲部落格鬥的目的，而且是為了娶到新娘，不是保護新娘；(B) 照抄第 1 段的 ritual，但第 2 段說卡波耶拉一開始是奴隸用來自衛的武術，歌舞是後來用來掩飾的。

questions.prompt: Why did Jeanie Low invent the Kiddie Stool, according to the passage?

options.A: Many other five-year-olds had problems reaching the bathroom sink.
options.B: She did not think that plastic stools were tall enough for her.
options.C: The stool in her bathroom was not firm and often got in the way.
options.D: She was invited to enter an invention contest held by her school.

questions.explanation: 第 1 段說 Jeanie 家裡的塑膠踏凳不穩（unstable），又讓小浴室很擠（cluttered up），選項換成 not firm 和 often got in the way。(D) 照抄 invention contest held by her school，學校的發明比賽是她動手做的契機，她要解決的是凳子不穩又占空間的問題，而且原文說她決定參加，不是受邀參加；(A) 照抄 five-year-olds，原文只說她和許多五歲小孩一樣要踩凳子，沒說其他小孩有困難；(B) 照抄 plastic，原文沒說塑膠凳不夠高。

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is true about how the Kiddie Stool works?

options.A: The Kiddie Stool will swing out only when the cabinet door opens.
options.B: It uses hinges and magnets to keep the wooden pieces in place.
options.C: It swings from left to right to be attached to the cabinet door.
options.D: The platform is supported by two pieces of metal.

questions.explanation: 第 2 段說 Jeanie 用金屬鉸鏈把兩片木板接起來，不用時鉸鏈讓木板摺回櫃門上，再用磁鐵固定（held in place by magnets），選項換成 uses hinges and magnets to keep the wooden pieces in place。(A) 照抄 cabinet door，凳子是從櫃門上往外展開，原文沒說要先打開櫃門；(C) 照抄 swing，原文說第一片木板水平展開、第二片往下擺，不是左右擺動；(D) 照抄 metal，金屬做的是鉸鏈，支撐平台的是兩片木板。

questions.prompt: What are the characteristics of Jeanie’s Kiddie Stool?

options.A: Permanent and foldable.
options.B: Fragile and eye-catching.
options.C: Conventional and touching.
options.D: Convenient and recyclable.

questions.explanation: 第 1 段說 Jeanie 要做一張固定在浴室裡（permanent fixture）、不用時又能收起來的凳子；第 2 段說不用時兩片木板能摺回櫃門上（fold back），選項換成 Permanent and foldable。(D) 照抄第 2 段的 convenient，方便說對了一半，但 recyclable 可回收文章沒提；(B) fragile 脆弱，和原文說的 sturdy 穩固正好相反；(C) touching 感人說的是第 3 段大家對這個故事的感受，conventional 傳統的也和新發明接不上。

questions.prompt: Which of the following sayings best captures the spirit of Jeanie Low’s story?

options.A: Failure is the mother of success.
options.B: There’s nothing new under the sun.
options.C: Necessity is the mother of invention.
options.D: Genius is 1% inspiration and 99% perspiration.

questions.explanation: 第 1 段說 Jeanie 因為家裡的凳子不穩又占空間，才想做一張更好的凳子；第 2 段說她怎麼做出兒童凳；第 3 段說兒童凳得獎、激勵許多人。整個故事是生活上有需要，才催生了發明，最貼切的是 (C) 需要為發明之母。(A) 失敗為成功之母，Jeanie 的發明一路得獎，文章沒有寫到失敗；(B) 太陽底下沒有新鮮事，和她做出新發明的故事不合；(D) 天才是 1% 的靈感加 99% 的汗水，強調的是苦幹，文章結尾強調的卻是想像力；三個選項都偏離主題。

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of this passage?

options.A: Treatments do not always cause harmful side effects.
options.B: Patients tend to believe more testing is better treatment.
options.C: Too much medical care may not be beneficial to patients.
options.D: Doctors generally recommend office visits that are necessary.

questions.explanation: 第 1 段開門見山：很多人相信醫療越多越好，但過度醫療可能造成傷害；第 2、3 段用 Power 太太的例子說明，太多檢查讓她身心受苦、幾乎破產，停掉例行檢查後病情反而穩定。全文要說的是太多醫療對病人未必有益，所以是 (C)。(B) 病人相信檢查越多越好，只是第 1 段第一句的說法，過於狹隘；(A) 說治療不一定有副作用、(D) 說醫生通常只建議必要的回診，都和文章的立場相反，偏離主題。

questions.prompt: Which of the following was a problem for Mrs. Power during her medical treatment?

options.A: She had to be hospitalized for three weeks whenever she had a cold.
options.B: She didn’t have any insurance, so she went broke because of her illness.
options.C: When test results showed she was fine, her doctor still ordered more tests.
options.D: Her doctor asked her to consult other specialists due to her constant complaints.

questions.explanation: 第 2 段說就算檢查結果正常（tests came back negative），醫生還是安排更多檢查，選項換成 test results showed she was fine 和 still ordered more tests。(A) 照抄 three weeks，原文說每三週回診一次，感冒住院是為了預防萬一，沒說住院三週；(D) 照抄 specialists，原文說連小毛病（minor complaints）也轉診，不是因為她一直抱怨；(B) 原文說醫療費用讓這對夫妻幾乎破產，沒提到有沒有保險。

questions.prompt: Who does “they” in the third paragraph most likely refer to?

options.A: Physicians.
options.B: Other patients.
options.C: Mr. and Mrs. Power.
options.D: The online support groups.

questions.explanation: they 出現在 Power 先生說的話裡：很難判斷 they 什麼時候越過了界線（crossed the line）。第 2 段一路寫的是醫生堅持回診、一再安排檢查和轉診，做得太多、越過界線的是醫生，所以是 (A)。(B) 照抄前一句的 other patients，(D) 照抄 online support groups，這對夫妻是和其他病友交流之後才開始質疑，病友和互助團體不是安排檢查的人；(C) Power 夫婦是承受過度醫療的一方。

questions.prompt: Which of the following best describes the author’s attitude toward medical tests?

options.A: More tests than necessary are too much.
options.B: Medical tests are essential for disease prevention.
options.C: Many tests are needed for confirmation of diagnosis.
options.D: Doctors’ interpretations of test results are seldom wrong.

questions.explanation: 第 1 段說過度醫療（太多掃描、太多抽血、太多醫療程序）可能造成傷害，一項檢查常會引出更多檢查；Power 太太的例子也說明檢查做得太多反而傷身又傷財，停掉例行檢查後病情穩定。作者認為超過需要的檢查就是太多了，所以是 (A)。(B)、(C) 強調檢查必要，和作者的立場相反；(D) 文章沒有談醫生判讀檢查結果準不準。

questions.prompt: What does Zeke Emanuel have in mind when saying “What did Mom put in the cereal?”

options.A: The secret to bringing up successful kids.
options.B: The recipe for a breakfast food.
options.C: The difference among the brothers.
options.D: The questions from his kids.

questions.explanation: 第 3 段說書出版後很多人來問：媽媽到底在麥片裡放了什麼？後面緊接著說三兄弟都很成功，而且在不同的領域。大家問的不是麥片，而是媽媽做了什麼，才養出三個成功的兒子，所以是 (A) 教出成功孩子的祕訣。(B) 只看字面，把 cereal 當成真的早餐；(D) 照抄 questions，這些問題是別人來問 Zeke 的，Zeke 的孩子是他寫故事的對象；(C) 三兄弟各在不同領域是問題的背景，大家想知道的是成功的原因。

questions.prompt: What does Zeke Emanuel think of the modern conveniences mentioned in the interview?

options.A: Better late than never.
options.B: Practice makes perfect.
options.C: One can live without many of them.
options.D: They are great inventions.

questions.explanation: 第 7 段 Zeke 說自己沒有電視、沒有車、不用臉書、不發推特；第 9 段說手機從四支減到兩支，還說了 thankfully（還好）。他少了這些東西照樣過日子，甚至樂於減少，所以是 (C) 很多東西沒有也能過活。(A) 遲做總比不做好、(B) 熟能生巧這兩句諺語和他的生活方式接不上；(D) 他不用這些東西，看不出他認為這些是偉大的發明。

questions.prompt: According to Zeke Emanuel, which of the following is a reason for the brothers’ success?

options.A: They defend themselves by attacking others.
options.B: They learn a lot from great people’s quotes.
options.C: They are committed to glorifying their parents.
options.D: They keep moving forward even after a big success.

questions.explanation: 第 5 段說第二個重點是永遠不因上一次的勝利停下來（never rest on the last victory），要做的事永遠還有，選項換成 keep moving forward even after a big success。(B) 照抄 quotes，put success in quotes 是把「成功」加上引號，表示他不敢自稱成功，不是向名人的名言學習；(A) 父親說的攻擊是最好的防禦，意思是主動出擊、不放棄，Zeke 接著就說「我們不放棄」，不是靠攻擊別人保護自己；(C) 母親給他們的是讓世界更好的期許，文章沒說三兄弟要替父母增光。

questions.prompt: Which of the following best summarizes Zeke Emanuel’s response to the last question?

options.A: The brothers look forward to a family trip on a cruise.
options.B: Nothing much will change in the near future for them.
options.C: Higher positions and more power will be their goals.
options.D: None of the brothers will go to the beach.

questions.explanation: 訪問者最後問五年後兄弟三人會在哪裡，Zeke 回答：Ari 還是經營同一家公司，Rahm 應該還是芝加哥市長，自己大概還是當學者。三個人都繼續做現在的事，所以是 (B) 近期不會有什麼改變。(A) 照抄 cruise，原文說的正好相反，三兄弟沒有人會去搭郵輪；(D) 照抄 beach，沒有人會坐在海灘上喝調酒，是用來說明他們不會停下來享樂，只是回答裡的一個細節，不能代表整段的意思；(C) Zeke 沒說三兄弟要追求更高的職位和權力。

questions.prompt: What was the first piece of man-made space trash?

options.A: A camera.
options.B: A tool kit.
options.C: A fuel tank.
options.D: A broken satellite.

questions.explanation: 第 2 段說第一件太空垃圾出現在 1964 年，是停止運作（stopped operating）、和地面失去聯繫的美國衛星先鋒一號，選項換成 a broken satellite。另外三個選項都照抄第 3 段：(A) 相機、(B) 工具箱、(C) 燃料箱是目前繞著地球的各種垃圾，不是第一件。

questions.prompt: Why were scientists NOT concerned about space trash in the beginning?

options.A: It no longer served any useful purpose.
options.B: It was millions of miles away from the Earth.
options.C: It did not cause any problems.
options.D: It was regarded as similar to comets and stars.

questions.explanation: 第 2 段說先鋒一號一直繞著地球運行，沒有造成任何後果（without any consequences），科學家才越來越習慣把東西丟著不管，選項換成 did not cause any problems。(A) 照抄 no longer served any useful purpose，這是在說科學家丟掉的是什麼東西，不是他們不擔心的原因；(D) 照抄第 1 段的 comets and stars，那是一般人以為太空裡只有的東西，和科學家的想法無關；(B) 文章沒說垃圾離地球幾百萬英里。

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is true about space junk?

options.A: It is huge, heavy machines.
options.B: It never changes position.
options.C: It floats slowly around the Earth.
options.D: It may cause problems for space shuttles.

questions.explanation: 第 4 段說太空垃圾的主要問題是可能撞上衛星、損壞航行中的太空船（damage traveling spacecraft），地面站監測垃圾也是為了防止垃圾撞上太空梭，選項換成 may cause problems for space shuttles。(A) 照抄第 3 段的 huge，原文說垃圾小到油漆碎片、大到燃料箱都有，不全是巨大的機器；(C) 照抄 around the Earth，垃圾確實繞著地球運行，但第 3 段說速度最高每小時 17,500 英里，不是慢慢飄；(B) 垃圾一直繞著地球轉，位置當然會改變。

questions.prompt: What has been done about the space trash problem?

options.A: Scientists have cleaned up most of the trash.
options.B: Large pieces of space trash are being closely watched.
options.C: Many nations have worked together to stop polluting space.
options.D: Ground stations are built to help store the trash properly in space.

questions.explanation: 題幹問的是已經做了什麼（What has been done），第 4 段只有地面站監測體積較大的垃圾是已經做到的（have been built），選項把 monitor 換成 closely watched。(C) 照抄 nations、(A) 照抄 clean：各國合作停止亂丟垃圾、清理已經在太空的垃圾，原文說是未來的計畫（Future plans），還沒做到；(D) 照抄 Ground stations，地面站是用來監測垃圾，不是在太空裡存放垃圾。

questions.prompt: What is this passage mainly about?

options.A: The evolution of traffic control systems.
options.B: The inventors of traffic lights in history.
options.C: The functions of different traffic signals.
options.D: The development of modern transportation.

questions.explanation: 第 1 段講 Knight 仿照鐵路號誌設計出交通號誌，第 2 段講這套號誌裝在倫敦一個月就因為瓦斯外洩爆炸停用，第 3 段講美國各大城跟進，Potts 再加上黃燈成為三色號誌，第 4 段講自駕車出現後號誌可能不再需要。文章裡沒有一句話直接點出全文的主旨，可是四段依時間往下排，合起來講的就是交通號誌系統怎麼演變。(B) 發明者只寫到 Knight 和 Potts 兩位，(C) 各種號誌代表什麼意思只在第 1、3 段帶到，都過於狹隘；(D) 文章只講號誌，沒講整個現代交通運輸，太過廣泛。

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is true, according to the passage?

options.A: Knight was injured in the explosion of his traffic light.
options.B: Potts’ traffic light was the first one to appear in the USA.
options.C: The first traffic signal originated from the idea of a traffic director.
options.D: Future vehicles may not need traffic lights to cross an intersection.

questions.explanation: 自駕車在選項換成 Future vehicles，「號誌不再必要」換成「可能不需要紅綠燈」。(A) 照抄第 2 段的 explosion，但受傷的是操作號誌的警察，不是 Knight；(C) 照抄第 1 段的 traffic director，原文說的是號誌臂像交通指揮的手勢，構想其實來自鐵路號誌；(B) 黃燈是改良，不是美國第一座。

questions.prompt: Here is a sentence: “This design was adopted in later traffic light designs across the world.” Which paragraph is most suitable to have it as the final sentence?

options.A: Paragraph 1.
options.B: Paragraph 2.
options.C: Paragraph 3.
options.D: Paragraph 4.

questions.explanation: This design 要接一個前面剛講完的設計，而且是之後世界各地都採用的；第 3 段最後一句的三色系統正好符合，今天的紅綠燈就是紅、黃、綠三色。(A) 第 1 段結尾講的是警察在旁邊操作號誌，而且第 2 段說這套號誌一個月後就停用了，談不上之後世界各地都採用；(B) 第 2 段結尾是英國禁用號誌，(D) 第 4 段講的是未來可能不再需要號誌，都接不上 later designs。

questions.prompt: What question does the passage answer?

options.A: How was the word “hula-hooping” derived?
options.B: Why did Wham-O start making hula hoops?
options.C: Where did Hawaiian hula dancing come from?
options.D: What was the favorite toy of ancient Egyptian kids?

questions.explanation: 第 2 段說明 hula 來自夏威夷的草裙舞，和 hoop 結合成 hula hooping，回答了這個詞怎麼來的。(C) 照抄 Hawaiian，但文章只說英國水手在夏威夷看到草裙舞，沒說草裙舞從哪裡來；(B) 只說 Wham-O 推出塑膠呼拉圈，沒說原因；(D) 只說埃及兒童玩圈圈，沒說那是最喜歡的玩具。

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is true about use of the hoop in history?

options.A: The British used it for medical purposes.
options.B: Native Americans used it to train animals.
options.C: Ancient Greeks used it as a tool for workout.
options.D: Hawaiian dancers used it to represent the circle of life.

questions.explanation: 希臘人的圈圈也是運動器材，exercise device 在選項換成 a tool for workout。(A) 照抄第 2 段的 medical，但醫療紀錄記的是玩圈圈玩到受傷；(B) 照抄第 3 段的 animals，但圈圈是用來象徵動物，不是訓練動物；(D) 照抄 circle of life，但那是北美原住民，不是夏威夷舞者。

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT mentioned as a way of enjoying hula hoop fun?

options.A: Striking.
options.B: Twirling.
options.C: Spinning.
options.D: Kicking.

questions.explanation: 有提到的三種玩法，選項都把原文的動詞改成動名詞：twirled 是 (B) Twirling，struck 是 (A) Striking，spun 是 (C) Spinning。用腳踢圈圈文章沒提。

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what materials have been used for making hoops?

options.A: reed, grapevine, bamboo, plastic
options.B: reed, grapevine, plastic, metal
options.C: reed, bamboo, plastic, animal skin

questions.explanation: 四種材料散在三段：埃及的葡萄藤、希臘的金屬、北美原住民的蘆葦、Wham-O 的塑膠。選項照用原文的材料名稱，竹子和獸皮文章都沒提：(A) 有竹子，(C) 有竹子和獸皮，(D) 有獸皮。

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of this passage?

options.A: To argue for the benefits of nopales.
options.B: To introduce a new source of energy.
options.C: To predict the future agriculture policy of Mexico.
options.D: To change people’s ideas about energy consumption.

questions.explanation: 第 1 段最後一句點出仙人掌的新用途：生產再生能源，後面幾段接著講沼氣發電機、試驗計畫、比其他作物好的地方和未來的展望，所以全文在介紹一種新的能源來源。(A) 第 4 段確實列出仙人掌比其他生質作物好的地方，但那只是其中一段，過於狹隘；(C) 墨西哥未來的農業政策、(D) 改變大家對能源消耗的看法，文章都沒有談，偏離主題。

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements about the prickly pear cactus is true?

options.A: Its soft inner part is often discarded.
options.B: It was not discovered until the modern era.
options.C: It turns into 200,000 tons of waste in Mexico each year.
options.D: It appears in a prominent place on Mexico’s national flag.

questions.explanation: prime spot 在選項換成 prominent place。(A) 照抄第 2 段的 soft inner，但丟掉的是外皮，嫩肉一直都在吃；(C) 照抄 200,000 tons，那是每年的產量，每天的廢棄物是 10 噸；(B) 照抄 modern，原文說古代阿茲特克人就把仙人掌視為神聖。

questions.prompt: What advantage does the prickly pear cactus have over other biofuel crops?

options.A: It generates more energy.
options.B: It will not influence food prices.
options.C: It may replace feed for livestock.
options.D: It can increase global food production.

questions.explanation: 不會對糧食價格造成壓力，在選項換成不會影響糧食價格。(D) 照抄 food production，但原文說的是不會和糧食生產搶水搶地，不是增加糧食產量。(A) 文章沒有比較仙人掌和其他作物哪個發的電比較多；(C) 文章也沒提到牲畜的飼料，第 4 段說仙人掌的果肉仍然留給人吃。
